# `Browser.Notification.Internals`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Browser.Notification.Internals — the low-level notification port surface:
the closed outbound/inbound ADTs and the raw `Ipe.Ffi.Js` request/subscribe
wiring the high-level `Ipe.Browser.Notification` layer wraps.

Importing this submodule discloses the same `js-port:notification` axis as the
top-level module (the disclosure is keyed on the `Ipe.Browser.Notification` path
prefix), so the raw port surface cannot be reached undisclosed.

## `Options`

The `Notification` display payload, mirroring the Web API `Notification`
constructor subset carried across the seal:

  * `title` — the notification's title line.
  * `body` — the notification's body text (may be empty).
  * `tag` — a grouping id; a later notification with the same `tag` replaces
    the earlier one rather than stacking (empty means no grouping).

Crossing the seal as a single record keeps the outbound variant single-payload:
`Show options` externally tags as `{ Show: { title, body, tag } }`.

## `defaults`

```ipe
defaults : String -> Options
```

The default payload for a bare `notify title`: the given title, no body, no
grouping tag.

## `JsCmd`

The ONE closed OUTBOUND port type: the whole outbound surface as a single
auditable object.

  * `RequestPermission` — ask the host to grant notification permission.
  * `Show options` — display a notification (requires a prior grant).

## `JsMsg`

The NARROW closed INBOUND port type for the `outcomes` subscription —
deliberately NOT the app's internal `Msg`. Every variant the browser can push
on the display path is enumerated, so the fold in the high-level layer is
EXHAUSTIVE and a denial can never be silently dropped: it becomes a typed
`Err`. The correlated `requestPermission` reply uses the separate
`PermissionReply` type, so `Shown` cannot stand in for a permission grant.

  * `Granted` — the host granted notification permission.
  * `Denied` — the host refused notification permission.
  * `Shown` — a notification was displayed.
  * `Unavailable` — the Notification API is absent in this context.

## `PermissionReply`

The closed reply vocabulary of a `RequestPermission` request — a SEPARATE
type from `JsMsg` so a display acknowledgement (`Shown`) has NO representation
as a permission outcome. A permission request resolves to exactly one of:

  * `PermGranted` — the host granted notification permission.
  * `PermDenied` — the host refused notification permission.
  * `PermUnavailable` — the Notification API is absent in this context.

Because the type omits any display-ack variant, the permission fold cannot map
a `Shown` frame to a grant even if the first-party glue misroutes one: an
unrecognised reply fails the correlated decode closed (the frame is dropped).

## `request`

```ipe
request : JsCmd -> Cmd.Cmd msg
```

`request cmd` — hand a closed outbound `JsCmd` to the raw port transport.
The served first-party JS sink reaches the `Notification` API; the reply
arrives inbound as a `JsMsg`.

## `requestOne`

```ipe
requestOne : JsCmd -> Task Error PermissionReply
```

`requestOne cmd` — correlated one-shot permission `JsCmd` → `Task Error
PermissionReply`. Routes through `Js.request` with the `permissionInbound`
decoder, whose closed vocabulary omits the display-ack event: a `shown` frame
misrouted onto a permission reply is decoded closed (the frame is dropped),
never a grant.

## `subscribe`

```ipe
subscribe : (JsMsg -> msg) -> Sub.Sub msg
```

`subscribe toMsg` — the inbound subscription over the fail-closed seal
decoder. `inbound` IS the security gate; a malformed / mismatched frame is
dropped whole. A decoded `JsMsg` is handed to `toMsg`.

## `inbound`

```ipe
inbound : Decode.Decoder JsMsg
```

The total, fail-closed decoder for a `JsMsg` frame of this capability.

It first requires the frame's `tag` to be `portTag`, so a frame of another
capability, or an untagged one, fails closed; the rest decodes as `inboundBody`.

## `permissionInbound`

```ipe
permissionInbound : Decode.Decoder PermissionReply
```

The total, fail-closed decoder for a `PermissionReply` frame of this capability.

It first requires the frame's `tag` to be `portTag`, so a frame of another
capability, or an untagged one, fails closed; the rest decodes as `permissionInboundBody`.
